posts.summary: OpenAI faces existential threat due to unsustainable spending and revenue deceleration

posts.text:
OpenAI's death will have dire consequences for those who've invested in the company, those who built its infrastructure, and, ultimately, everyone else. And it's time to acknowledge the danger ahead.

posts.text:
What follows is anyone's guess. OpenAI might be absorbed into Microsoft. It might be allowed to die, with Altman becoming the sacrificial lamb for the AI bubble, or (chaos bet) it might merge with arch-enemy Anthropic. Either way, it's the end.

posts.quote:

posts.text:

posts.summary: Additional funding rounds or IPO cannot fix OpenAI's fundamentally broken business model
posts.quote:
We might see one final round, possibly a down round, to keep OpenAI afloat for a few more months. Or, there might be a rushed IPO. None of these would change OpenAI's horrendous (and fatal) fundamentals)

posts.text:
I believe the beginning of the end for OpenAI will come when it misses a revenue target, or shows major signs of deceleration. Any guidance restatements from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, CoreWeave or Cerebras are the pale horses to watch out for.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: Revenue target misses or deceleration signals will trigger OpenAI's collapse
posts.quote:
I believe the beginning of the end for OpenAI will come when it misses a revenue target, or shows major signs of deceleration. Any guidance restatements from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, CoreWeave or Cerebras are the pale horses to watch out for.

posts.text:
I don't know when OpenAI will die. I do know that a company whose existence hinges on its ability to continually raise ever-larger funding rounds, and that is deeply unprofitable, will eventually run out of time.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: Unprofitable company dependent on continuous mega-funding rounds will inevitably fail
posts.quote:
I don't know when OpenAI will die. I do know that a company whose existence hinges on its ability to continually raise ever-larger funding rounds, and that is deeply unprofitable, will eventually run out of time.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...

posts.text:
A huge part of the problem is that OpenAI's on-paper valuation is too damn high, and if it went public today, its debut price wouldn't be that much bigger. What, exactly, is in it for a VC looking for even a 2x or 3x return?

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: OpenAI's valuation too high; insufficient returns available to attract venture capital
posts.quote:
A huge part of the problem is that OpenAI's on-paper valuation is too damn high, and if it went public today, its debut price wouldn't be that much bigger. What, exactly, is in it for a VC looking for even a 2x or 3x return?

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...

posts.text:
The scale of OpenAI's capital needs is such that I don't see private credit or VC being able to fill the gap. Asset managers already struggled to raise the funds behind NVIDIA's fake $500bn "fund" - $100bn+ a year in private funding ain't gonna happen.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: Private markets cannot raise sufficient capital for OpenAI's massive annual funding needs
posts.quote:
The scale of OpenAI's capital needs is such that I don't see private credit or VC being able to fill the gap. Asset managers already struggled to raise the funds behind NVIDIA's fake $500bn "fund" - $100bn+ a year in private funding ain't gonna happen.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...

posts.text:
OpenAI needs capital like you and I need oxygen to survive. The problem is that the vast majority of its last two funding rounds came from SoftBank, Amazon and NVIDIA - who either can't afford to or don't want to invest any further. 

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: OpenAI's major funders cannot or unwilling to provide further investment

posts.text:
And OpenAI's spending commitments *are* insane. As I noted in my last newsletter, it's on the hook for over $800bn by the end of the decade, with an estimated $146bn due through the end of 2027 across Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: OpenAI's $800bn spending commitments make financial survival mathematically implausible
posts.quote:
And OpenAI's spending commitments *are* insane. As I noted in my last newsletter, it's on the hook for over $800bn by the end of the decade, with an estimated $146bn due through the end of 2027 across Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...

posts.text:
Growth is only one part of the problem. OpenAI's business sucks. It's deeply unprofitable, and it's made insane spending commitments that require it to raise hundreds of billions each year. It needs to raise at least $100bn a year through 2030.

posts.quote:

posts.text:
OpenAI has been outpaced by Anthropic - it took until August to be "on track" to hit $40bn in run rate (a useless metric, but still), a number that Anthropic beat by $7bn in May. Catching up will be difficult, because the era of token-maxxing is over.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: Anthropic surpassing OpenAI in revenue; OpenAI falling behind in competitive race
posts.quote:

posts.text:
If Anthropic beats OpenAI to the public markets, it's over, primarily because as bad as Anthropic's numbers might be, OpenAI's are worse, all while having $500 billion more in obligations and a chaotic mix of different products.

www.wheresyoured.at/what-happens...
posts.summary: Anthropic IPO before OpenAI would seal OpenAI's fate due to worse financials
posts.quote:

posts.text:
